segments.text: Oreck’s arrows flew—green chroniton trails cutting precise arcs.
Halvar charged—a silent avalanche of muscle and fury.
His blade sliced through Reptilian spines before they turned.
Shieldbearers surged forward, locking overlapping barriers as Igigi scattered in confusion.
Mika’s lance became a conductor’s baton, directing Legionnaires to isolate each spire.
Luminaire’s song surged through Geralt, pure and furious.
He plunged his gauntlet into the corrupted Nexus pool.
Cold fire raced up his arm—Anunnaki rot fighting Earth’s heartbeat.
Black tendrils lashed, tearing at his soul. *"Pour it back!"* Luminaire cried.
Geralt roared, pouring five hundred Legion souls’ harmonic will through the gauntlet.
Gold light erupted, incinerating the darkness.
For a heartbeat, the Garden breathed free.
Luminaire sighed: *"Anchor... held..."* But reptilian horns blared in the distance.
Gate destabilizing!" Geralt ripped his gauntlet from the cleansed Nexus.
Silver light already engulfed the Legion—transit energy fraying at the edges.
Homeward sigil—now!" Oreck’s arrows traced the dragonway glyph in emerald flame.
Legionnaires locked shields, vrill-chant rising to a crescendo.
Luminaire’s light pulsed weakly. *"Mars... calling..."* Earth’s gravity tugged.
Distant reptilian screams choked into silence as silver consumed sight.
Geralt’s last glimpse: Igigi survivors vanishing into ferns, their eyes wide with dawning hope.
Dragon Nebula light bathed the Legion in sapphire gloom.
Luminara’s spire stood whole again—obsidian gleaming under alien stars.
Luminaire sighed within Geralt’s palm: *"Duty... fulfilled."* Relief warred with exhaustion.
Oreck lowered his bow, fingers trembling.
Earth resonance stable." But Geralt felt it—the Nebula’s watchful gaze.
He tightened his grip on Luminara’s fading warmth.
And four storm-lit figures lingered in memory—lightning fists, star-woven robes, shadows that killed.
Victory tasted like ashes and ozone.
Where Geralt remembered mist-laced calm, now humid air vibrated with predatory awareness—a sentient pressure against his eardrums.
Canopy gaps revealed pyramids swallowed by writhing vines that pulsed faint crimson beneath moss, like infected arteries.
Reptilian shrieks echoed not from distance, but from camouflaged emitters woven into strangler figs.
Anunnaki tech wasn’t just reactivated; it had metastasized into the ecosystem itself.
Vrill-energy, once Earth’s song, now thrummed as a weaponized drone.
Luminara shuddered in Geralt’s palm, her light guttering. *"Roots... digging deep..."*
Oreck vanished into a curtain of phosphorescent creepers.
His salvaged armor—scavenged from Heavens wreck—hummed in perfect resonance with the pyramid’s defensive lattice.
To thermal scanners, he was background radiation.
To Geralt’s enhanced senses, he moved like a ghost tracing fault lines: here, a buried power conduit; there, a sonic tripwire disguised as orchid pollen.
His bowstring glowed emerald, charged by stolen energy.
He knew where the nexus hid—not in the central chamber, but beneath the sacrificial altar, where agony amplified the signal.
And the Anunnaki weren’t building fortresses.
They were grafting themselves onto Earth’s bones.
Halvar crouched beside a petrified log, nostrils flaring.
Fresh." Mika’s lance tip trembled—not from exhaustion, but rage.
Below, through cracked basalt, faint crimson light illuminated cages stacked like cordwood.
Igigi prisoners huddled inside, their vrill-dampening collars flickering.
Reptilian guards patrolled above, claws clicking on stone fused with crystalline cabling.
Reinforcements inbound." Geralt’s command was a blade-honed whisper: "Oreck.
Sentinel trees shifted, bark splitting to reveal gunmetal apertures.
he thought, nocking an arrow tipped with stolen chroniton energy. The air screamed. Violet light erupted from the sphere—too late. Oreck released. Emerald met entropy. The world tore open.
Aboveground, Geralt felt the shockwave through his boots.
Cascade effect—all local nodes failing!" Halvar grinned, teeth bloody in twilight.
Mika slammed her lance down, shield-wall flaring silver.
Reptilian guards stumbled, their control collars sparking.
Her light spluttered, then flared—gold bleeding through jungle gloom.
Yet Geralt knew: Oreck’s strike was a scalpel, not a cure.
Beneath the altar, the nexus sphere shattered.
Oreck rolled aside as violet backlash scorched stone.
Green light bled from his armor—camouflage failing.
He scrambled up rubble, bow humming.
A shadow filled the doorway—taller than memory, armored in obsidian scales.
His finger slipped on the bowstring.
Sub-Level Bio-Signature—Oreck’s vitals spiking!" Geralt spun.
Betrayed.* Halvar snarled, already moving toward the pyramid’s hidden entrance.
Now!" But vines snapped shut, sealing the entrance.
Serpentor’s laughter echoed through tremoring earth.
The armor’s stolen resonance flickered, then died.
Yet Oreck’s gaze dropped to the altar rubble.
A memory surfaced—training drills on Martian dunes. *When resonance fails, fracture the harmonics.* He slammed his palm into a fragment.
Oreck rolled—snatched the fallen arrow—impaled the fragment into the altar’s central vein.
The explosion wasn’t fire—it was silence.
All local systems destabilizing!" Geralt felt it—a tremor through Luminara.
Luminara dimmed. *Roots... deeper...* Victory tasted bitter.
Her light traced crimson emitters in writhing vines.
Vrill-lines pulsed, bleeding violet energy toward distant peaks.
Mika whispered: "They're feeding the network." Lyra’s scanner hissed.
Node Gamma... regenerating." Oreck choked out words: "Weakening roots.
Cut one... others compensate." He touched a vine.
Emerald light bled through corrupted veins.
Gold-black nexus fragments seeped into stone.
"Primary node... underground... beneath the altar." Halvar grinned—blood on teeth.
The Garden awakened—and it remembered vengeance.
Geralt’s first warning wasn’t the crimson pulse beneath the vines but the alien disgust coiling through his neural link.
The Applicator—usually humming with detached analysis—spat diagnostics like poison: *“Vrill resonance inverted.
Cognitive corruption: Truth reframed as suggestion.
Memory malleation event likely.”* This wasn’t integration.
Above, the Legion advanced through suffocating green twilight.
Private Ren froze beside a dripping fern.
His hand trembled near his blade.
"They’re slowing down for *me*," he muttered, eyes darting at Halvar’s broad back.
Ren’s whisper echoed back, colder: "They’ll leave you behind... just like on Mars." His knuckles whitened.
He knew the source—the grafted vrill whispering through root-filaments—yet the dread felt *his*, marrow-deep and shameful.
Geralt’s Applicator flared hot behind his temple.
Halvar’s shoulders tensed beside him—not at Reptilian claws scraping stone, but at the whispers threading through dripping fronds.
Private Ren’s blade trembled near a pulsing vine.
"They’re slowing down for *me*," the Legionnaire choked.
The vine answered in Ren’s own voice, colder: "Just like Mars." Ren’s knuckles whitened.
He knew the source—the grafted vrill was a parasite in the air—yet the shame felt bone-deep. *His* failing. *His* abandonment.
Shieldbearers formed overlapping barriers, but the corruption slithered beneath.
An Igigi prisoner pressed against crystalline bars—his eyes vacant, lips moving: "The chains fit better now..." The vine above him crooned back: "Quiet is safety." Geralt felt Luminara shudder.
Her golden light trembled against encroaching violet.
Roots snaked across their path, throbbing like infected arteries.
Oreck’s salvaged armor sparked—emerald light flickering where it touched stone.
His fingers brushed a moss-slick obelisk.
Instantly, Senareth’s voice echoed: *"Endurance is surrender."* It wasn’t Senareth.
It was Oreck’s deepest fear—wrapped in his mentor’s timbre.
The sound amplified tenfold, swallowed by jungle laughter.
Through the neural link, Geralt tasted copper and salt—the sergeant’s memory-flash: Mars, sand choking his brother’s lungs.
Always too slow." Halvar roared—not in battle-fury, but anguish.
The Garden remembered pain, and now it weaponized regret.
It demanded belief in unraveling minds.
The jungle’s whispers thickened as twilight bled into deep violet gloom.
Halvar’s knuckles whitened around his axe handle; every rustling leaf echoed with his brother’s dying gasps from Mars.
"We stop *here*," Geralt commanded, slicing through the mental fog with Luminara’s flickering gold light.
The clearing was a trap—vines coiled like sleeping serpents, obelisks humming with inverted resonance—but exhaustion outweighed caution.
Legionnaires collapsed against petrified logs, eyes darting at shifting shadows.
Ren’s hand trembled near his blade.
"They’ll slit our throats while we sleep," he muttered.
The vine above him sighed back: "*Sleep is surrender.*"
Oreck traced glyphs in the damp soil—ancient Martian warding sigils.
His salvaged armor sputtered emerald light where it touched the symbols, pushing back the cognitive poison.
"The corruption targets doubt," he rasped, sweat stinging his eyes.
Anchor them." Mika knelt beside him, her lance plunged into soft earth.
Shield energy flared silver, carving a fragile dome of clarity.
Within it, the air tasted cleaner—pine and ozone instead of decay.
Yet outside, the jungle pulsed, alive with malice.
Distant Igigi whimpers twisted into accusations: "*You abandoned us.*"
Halvar paced the perimeter, axe gleaming.
"Focus on the weight," Geralt ordered, his Applicator scorching against his skull.
Hear my voice." Ren flinched as vines whispered his darkest shame—the Martian outpost he’d fled.
"They’re thorns, not truths." Luminara’s glow brightened, casting long, defiant shadows.
Around them, the Legionnaires clutched weapons, lips moving in silent mantras: names of home, rhythms of drills, equations of vrill-flow.
Resistance was a raw, scraping thing—a refusal to let their minds be unmade.
Deep in the undergrowth, obsidian eyes watched.
Three reptilian scouts, scales tuned to the corrupted harmonics, tasted the shield’s disruption.
Their claws flexed, ready to rend flesh *or* sanity.
Tomorrow, they’d cut deeper toward the heart—and rip the poison from its roots.
The jungle pressed closer, its whispers threading through the shield-dome like poisoned needles.
Halvar’s axe trembled—not from fatigue, but from the vine-murmur replaying his brother’s last rattling breath.
He slammed the blade into the soil, anchoring himself in the vibration.
"Focus on gravity." Legionnaires echoed the mantra, gripping weapons until knuckles bled white.
Ren’s eyelids fluttered as the corruption hissed: *Coward.
Weak.* He bit his tongue, tasting copper, and whispered his daughter’s name instead.
Violet light pulsed through veins in the leaves—Anunnaki tech feeding on doubt.
Shield integrity at 65%." Mika’s lance dug deeper into the earth, silver light fraying at the edges.
Oreck pressed his palm against a glyph-carved obelisk.
Emerald energy flared, pushing back the gloom.
"Twisting memory into traps." Senareth’s voice slithered from a nearby vine: *"You failed me."* Oreck snarled, shattering the stone with a chroniton-charged arrow.
Vines lashed like whips, thorns gleaming with venom.
Reptilian shadows detached from the trees, claws scraping stone.
Halvar roared, axe cleaving through scaled flesh.
Mika’s shield-wall flared, deflecting psychic shrieks that tasted of burnt ozone.
Her golden light seared through the violet haze, revealing three scouts—obsidian-scaled, eyes vacant—advancing with mechanical precision.
Legionnaires met them blade-to-claw, screams swallowed by the storm.
The Legionnaire saw Martian sand, his own retreating footsteps.
Then Geralt’s voice cut through: "Nowhere to run here." Ren’s blade found the creature’s throat.
In the lull, Oreck touched a dying scout’s armor.
Resonance flickered—a map of pain etched in vrill.
"The corruption flows *through* them." Geralt’s Applicator burned: *Parasitic symbiosis confirmed*.
Cut the scouts, and the roots would bleed.
Oreck crouched beside the scout's corpse.
His fingers brushed cold scales, syncing his salvaged armor.
Emerald light pulsed through the reptile's neural lattice—a fractal map of agony etched in vrill.
Parasite lines fed into distant nodes.
Pain amplifiers." Geralt's Applicator scalded his temple: VERIFIED.
TERMINATE HOSTS TO SEVER FEEDBACK LOOPS.
Halvar wiped black blood from his axe.
"So we kill the messengers?" His voice was gravel scraped raw.
Private Ren stared at his bloodied blade.
"Then—we're helping them?" The vine above him sighed: *Always helping.*
Mika's shield flared silver as another psychic shriek hit—burnt ozone and despair.
"How do we fight a forest that eats doubt?"
"We don't fight." He nocked it, aiming at the scout's twitching spine.
Instantly, the corpse *screamed*—not sound, but silence.
A vacuum that sucked the air from lungs.
Geralt felt it—a tremor through Luminara.
But his Applicator blazed crimson: WARNING: NODE GAMMA REACTIVATING.
Senareth's voice slithered from the ground: *You only delayed the harvest.*
Geralt stared at the scout's ashen scales. Black veins now glowed gold-*green*. The very hue of Oreck's arrow. "They *learned*."
Then the roots began to sing.
It started where Oreck’s chroniton arrow had struck—a low, dissonant hum vibrating through the scout’s corpse.
The gold-green veins pulsed like infected lightning, spreading through petrified wood and moss-slick stone.
Where the Legion stood, the ground trembled—not in threat, but in terrible imitation.
Vines uncoiled, lifting toward the canopy as if conducting an unseen orchestra.
The notes tasted of copper and spoiled honey on Geralt’s tongue.
Private Ren clapped hands over his ears.
"Make it stop—" His plea fractured into the jungle’s stolen timbre.
"—stop pretending you can save us!" The vines echoed, weaving his despair into harmony.
Shieldbearers stumbled back as Mika’s lance dimmed; the silver dome flickered, its light thinning against the rising chorus.
Halvar gripped his axe, knuckles pale.
Corruption adapting to chroniton frequency—" Her voice broke as the jungle whispered her own diagnosis back: *Adaptation equals extinction.* Geralt slammed Luminara’s base into the soil.
Golden light flared, searing vines that crept too close.
The applicator burned against his skull: PARASITE ISOLATING HOST NEURAL SIGNATURES.
But beneath the warning, a deeper truth shimmered: The green-gold veins weren’t just copying Oreck’s attack.
Oreck crouched beside the scout, fingers pressed to corrupted scales.
His armor synced—emerald light writhing against gold-green intrusion.
Through the neural link, Geralt felt it: fractal patterns unfolding like poisoned flowers.
"It’s rehearsal." Senareth’s voice coiled through the roots— *For the Garden’s requiem*.
Above them, winged shadows banked lower, their flight paths syncing to the dissonant hymn.
Geralt watched a vine stroke Ren’s trembling shoulder.
Her light carved a single, pure note into the cacophony.
A question only sorrow could answer.
For a heartbeat, the singing stuttered,
as if remembering it had no throat of its own.
From the fissure rose a serpentine root,
and humming with Ren’s stolen terror,
The Legion’s defiance echoed in the silence—
The root-monster swayed—a grotesque parody of breath.
Ren’s terror thrummed through its bark-carved emitters; Halvar’s guilt pulsed in the veins of its thorns.
It *listened*, drinking the Legion’s silence like poison wine.
Luminara’s gold light sputtered as the root hummed louder—not a battle cry, but a twisted chorus of their own voices.
Ren whimpered as it sang *"Coward"* in his daughter’s stolen lilt.
Halvar’s axe trembled; the vine mirrored his shaking grip.
"It’s reflecting us!" His armor flared emerald, but Node Gamma instantly bled gold-green—copying the frequency.
Geralt barked. Every counterattack became data for the parasite. He forced stillness. Luminara dimmed to a dying ember.
Dirt crumbled into the fissure as Node Gamma heaved upward, dripping acidic sap that hissed against Mika’s flickering shield.
The air reeked of ozone and rotting orchids.
A vine lashed toward Ren—slow, inquisitive.
It brushed his cheek, cold as reptilian scales.
He froze, tears carving paths through grime.
The vine tightened around Ren’s throat.
Node Gamma leaned in—a hunter savoring surrender.
In the suffocating quiet, Geralt’s Applicator flickered once:
Ren’s choked gasp echoed through the emitters—amplified into a shriek that shattered Mika’s shield-wall.
Acidic sap rained down as vines erupted from the fissure.
Geralt drove Luminara into the soil.
Her golden light flared—not against the root, but *through* it.
Node Gamma’s core pulsed crimson where Ren’s stolen memories bled.
Not toward the monster, but sideways—his axe carving sigils into stone Oreck had marked hours earlier.
Vines recoiled as ancestral geometry scorched their false flesh.
Not at the core, but into the soil where Node Gamma’s roots drank deep.
Chroniton energy bloomed downward—a temporal anchor dragging the parasite toward its own creation moment.
For a heartbeat, Geralt saw it: the Anunnaki drill biting into virgin earth fifteen years past.
Gold-green veins thickened, swallowing the chroniton pulse.
Node Gamma learned—adapting its resonance to mimic Oreck’s armor frequency.
The dissonance slammed Geralt to his knees.
Ren sobbed as roots pried open his mind, mining fresh despair.
Standing, he ripped the Applicator from his temple.
Blood streamed down his cheek as he pressed the scorching metal to Luminara’s haft.
The relic blazed—feeding on his pain, his doubt, the weight of every Legionnaire’s scream.
Her light shifted from gold to blinding white.
Node Gamma recoiled, emitters overloading as pure, unfiltered humanity flooded its circuits.
For the first time, the jungle screamed—not imitation, but agony.
Above them, wings dove through the canopy—too fast, too late.
The root twitched—not in retreat, but anticipation.
Here is the revised ending with the new twist about the Applicator — a rogue duplicate communicating with the hive, while the real one remains hidden and intact.
The blinding white light seared Geralt’s vision, throbbing against Node Gamma’s corrupted heart.
Acidic sap hissed where it struck vines, vaporizing into acrid clouds that stung the Legionnaires’ throats.
Through the glare, Geralt glimpsed the parasite’s core pulsing faster—not overwhelmed, but analyzing.
Its gold-green veins flared brighter, synchronizing with Luminara’s desperate resonance.
Ren crumpled to his knees, clutching his temples.
"Counting my breaths." The root echoed him perfectly: a thousand whispering vines replicating each ragged gasp.
Mika’s shield flickered back to life, silver light straining against the cognitive tide.
Halvar swung his axe—not at the root, but at the rune-carved earth.
Martian glyphs flared emerald beneath its twisting tendrils.
His arrow’s chroniton tip hummed with stolen time—the spark before impact.
He aimed low, beneath the root’s armored segments, toward threads binding it to the deeper network.
Geralt nodded, blood dripping from his temple onto Luminara’s haft.
The relic drank it greedily, light wavering between white and sickly gold-green imitation.
Reptilian scouts descended in silence, claws extended not for flesh, but for the fractured shield-dome.
Their scales vibrated with the jungle’s stolen chorus—Halvar’s guilt, Ren’s terror, Oreck’s faith—amplified into weapons.
Mika met them with lance raised, her defiance a raw scream swallowed by dissonance.
Senareth’s voice slithered through the roots once more: All gardens end.
"Not yet." Luminara pulsed—a final, searing note of pure defiance.
Node Gamma shuddered, emitters flaring crimson.
For a heartbeat, its song fractured into static.
Then the serpentine root lunged—not at Geralt, but at Oreck’s drawn bow.
But Geralt’s Applicator—the one fused to his temple—didn’t just analyze the attack.
A faint, encrypted pulse bled from his skull into the root’s core.
Node Gamma absorbed it instantly, its next movement preempting Oreck’s shot.
Emergency preservation tactics it began duplicity…
And it wasn’t just adapting to the hive.
Every tactical readout, every resonance scan, every flicker of Legionnaire fear—it had been streaming to Node Gamma.
The parasite wasn’t learning on its own.
Halvar roared, axe biting deep into a vine—but the vine had already hardened at the point of impact.
Geralt’s hand shot to his temple.
The duplicate Applicator resisted, bio-filaments tearing from his neural ports.
It shrieked in his mind—not a machine error, but a hive-alert.
Gold-green light bled from its casing as it came free, writhing in his grip like a caught insect.
For a second, he saw it clearly: a perfect replica, down to the wear on its edges.
But inside, its core glowed with the same venomous violet as the jungle’s emitters.
He crushed it against Luminara’s haft.
The duplicate sparked, died, and went dark.
Its song stuttered, emitters cycling through frequencies—searching for the feed that had just gone dead.
For the first time, it was truly alone.
And in that silence, Geralt’s real Applicator—the one buried in his occipital nerve cluster, dormant since Mars—booted up.
Just a clean, cold stream of data across his vision:
ANALYSIS: NODE GAMMA RESONANCE PATTERN LOCKED TO DUPLICATE PROTOCOLS.
PROTOCOL DELTA ENGAGED: COUNTER-RESONANCE MIRRORING READY.
The duplicate had been feeding the hive their strategies.
Now, the real Applicator would feed the hive its own.
Geralt’s voice cut through the stillness. “Here it is. Filtered. Weaponized.”
He let the real Applicator flood Node Gamma with a perfected, mirrored echo of everything the duplicate had sent—but inverted.
The parasite, trained on the duplicate’s data, couldn’t adapt.
Node Gamma screamed—a raw, mechanical shriek untouched by stolen souls.
Its gold-green veins blackened, seared by the truth of its own stolen logic.
Above, wings faltered, scouts tumbling from the sky as their harmonic link shattered.
The shield-dome flared pure silver, Mika’s lance blazing with renewed light.
His axe found the root’s core.
Dawn’s first light pierced the canopy.
The real war wasn’t just against the jungle.
It was against the lies they carried with them.
And Geralt’s real Applicator was now wide awake, listening not to the hive—
But for the next traitor in their midst.
